net_effect: The engagement-side numbers (activity, retention, segments, concentration) are reliable and computed directly from clean ledger data. The value-side numbers are structurally unable to answer monetary questions at Pool level - fixing this is the single highest data priority in the recommendations (R-3).

limitations.title: Scope: one contract, one chain, one six-month window
limitations.what: Every transaction against the Aave V3 Pool on Polygon between 2026-03-09 and 2026-09-05 (181 days). September is partial (through 09-05; 716 active wallets).
limitations.why_it_matters: Findings describe this contract on this chain in this window. They do not generalize to other Aave markets, other chains, or other periods. No forecast is attempted.
limitations.mitigation: Every number is scoped to this window and the partial September is flagged wherever it is cited.

limitations.title: Wallet addresses are not people
limitations.what: 'Active wallet' counts distinct addresses, not unique humans. One person can control many wallets; one wallet can be an automated agent.
limitations.why_it_matters: MAU, segmentation, and retention figures over- or understate the true user base depending on the multi-wallet/agent mix.
limitations.mitigation: The report uses 'wallet' and 'user' with that caveat in mind; the bot-like timing finding is explicitly hedged at Medium confidence because no wallet-fingerprinting was done.

limitations.title: Native value is degenerate - the central measurement gap
limitations.what: Aave positions move as ERC-20 aTokens, not as native POL. Pool-level native value attaches almost entirely to the Pool contract itself (1,065.51 POL received, effectively gas-refund mechanics), so wallets.total_volume and transactions.value_native are ~$0 for real users. Only 38 of 158,916 transactions carry native value; the median transaction value is 0 POL.
limitations.why_it_matters: Monetary KPIs (KPI-03/04/07), volume-by-segment, and value-based whale lists read near zero and would mislead anyone who takes them at face value.
limitations.mitigation: Recommended fix (R-3) is function-level decoding of supply/borrow/withdraw/repay calls plus a real-time POL/USD and aToken price reference. Until then value figures are reported as degenerate and the RFM segments are described as R x F driven.

limitations.title: Token transfers are mostly spam and un-priced
limitations.what: 156 of 163 token transfers are unverified spam airdrops. The warehouse stores no token decimals or prices for the remaining transfers.
limitations.why_it_matters: Token-level value cannot close the monetary gap; spam transfers are correctly excluded from activity and retention, but their parent transactions are not part of the Pool ledger by design.
limitations.mitigation: Spam is flagged (is_spam) and excluded from monetary fallback and activity; the residual gap is owned by R-3.

limitations.title: Failed, self, and zero-value transactions are counted
limitations.what: 4,514 of 158,916 transactions (2.84%) have status = 0. Failed, self, and zero-value rows are flagged - never dropped.
limitations.why_it_matters: Raw activity counts include failed attempts, slightly inflating demand-side numbers.
limitations.mitigation: They are isolated in flagged_transactions.csv and surfaced as an anomaly/risk input (BR-07) rather than silently hidden.

limitations.title: Automated / bot activity may inflate the base
limitations.what: The busiest wallet executed 8,054 transactions; activity clusters at 12:00 UTC on Thursdays with near-zero weekends. The Pool contract is the recipient of every transaction and is set aside only for user-level concentration analysis.
limitations.why_it_matters: MAU and transaction counts overstate organic retail usage; top-wallet dependency risk is real.
limitations.mitigation: The timing finding is labeled Medium confidence; bot addresses were not de-duplicated (flagged as future work in R-6).

limitations.title: Retention is transaction-based
limitations.what: A wallet is 'active' in a month only if it transacted. A holder or borrower with no on-chain activity that month is counted as inactive; native value is not a retention signal here.
limitations.why_it_matters: Month-1 retention (21.1% average) understates a value-holding base that interacts rarely; cohort results are engagement, not deposits.
limitations.mitigation: The definition is stated in kpi_framework.md (KPI-02) and methodology.md; real deposit-value retention requires R-3.

limitations.title: Cost figures use a daily price reference, and the ratio is meaningless
limitations.what: gas_cost_usd applies the daily CoinGecko POL/USD price (100% coverage in window). The gas-as-%-of-value measure divides gas by native value, which is degenerate; the value x gas correlation (r = -0.05, p = 0.78) is reported as non-meaningful.
limitations.why_it_matters: Absolute cost (~$0.0073/tx, ~$1,158 total) is reliable; any ratio or correlation that depends on native value is not.
limitations.mitigation: The report says this explicitly (Finding 3.4) and recommends re-measuring fee economics at function level after R-3.

limitations.title: Data-quality constraints from the V2 API
limitations.what: token_transfers.transfer_id is a surrogate (tx_hash + '_' + seq) because the V2 API omits logIndex; tokentx parent transactions are not in the Pool ledger; addresses are normalized to lowercase without case-checksum validation.
limitations.why_it_matters: Minor join/audit friction, no impact on counts.
limitations.mitigation: Documented in data_dictionary.md; referential integrity is verified on load (0 orphans).

limitations.title: Environment and reproducibility dependencies
limitations.what: The local PostgreSQL server runs in WSL2 and requires jit=off (missing LLVM runtime); fact_transactions.csv is large and gitignored; the .pbix is gitignored.
limitations.why_it_matters: Full reproduction needs a reachable PostgreSQL instance and the local Power BI files; the GitHub repo carries code + small extracts, not the raw data or the workbook.
limitations.mitigation: methodology.md section 6 gives the exact run order. The webapp itself needs none of this - it reads committed static JSON.

limitations.title: No off-chain context
limitations.what: Price feeds are market references, not user-reported intent; no marketing/financial events, support tickets, or survey data are available to explain why activity moved (e.g. the April 8-14 spike is inferred to be a promotional/airdrop event from on-chain timing alone).
limitations.why_it_matters: Causal explanations in the reports are hypotheses, not verified business events.
limitations.mitigation: The findings that rest on inference are labeled Medium confidence and competing explanations are noted (e.g. bot activity in Finding 3.5).
